topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of genetic susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising within susceptible cells can support clonal evolution in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental exposure, chance and population differences in cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how strongly environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk relative to chance and inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and host conditions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce mutagenic DNA damage through mechanisms shaped by their processing within the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from the promotion that enables initiated cells to proliferate and form tumours.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the consequences of carcinogen exposure depend on the biological context of the affected cells, then recap the mechanisms leading to that conclusion.

topics.label: Human evidence linking carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence collected from people and their cancer cells can connect particular exposures with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess how experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results may not capture cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing recaps the lecture's conclusions and places cancer-risk assessment within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
